access.title: Access
access.description: Who can log in to this database, and who on this platform can manage it.
access.unsupportedBody: This engine does not have managed database users yet. Platform access below still applies.
access.notRunningBody: Users are read from the live database. Start it to list, create or change logins.
access.loadFailed: Could not read this database's users: {{error}}

users.title: Database users
users.description: Logins on the database itself. Your apps keep using the platform's own credentials, so a user here never breaks them.
users.emptyBody: Create a read-only login for a teammate or a reporting tool instead of sharing the main password.

presetHint.read_only: Can read every table. Writes are refused even if a tool tries.
presetHint.read_write: Can read and change rows. Cannot change the schema.
presetHint.owner: Full control of this one database, including schema. No server level rights.

users.protectedNote: Platform role, cannot be changed here
users.rotateToast: Password rotated. Open sessions were ended.
users.deleteBody: The login is removed and its sessions end. Anything it created is kept and handed to the admin role.
users.rotateRestarted: Restarted to pick up the new credential: {{apps}}.

create.title: Create a database user
create.description: The password is generated and shown once. It is never stored, so copy it before closing.
create.name: User name
create.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
create.limitHint: Stops one tool from using every connection.

credential.title: Copy this now
credential.description: This password is shown once and is not stored anywhere. If you lose it, rotate the password.
credential.tlsNote: TLS is required by this connection string.

temp.title: Temporary credentials
temp.description: A short-lived login for a developer or a one-off job. It expires and is removed on its own, even if this control plane restarts.
temp.clampedNote: The lifetime was moved into the allowed range of {{min}} to {{max}} minutes.
temp.failedToast: Could not issue a temporary login

who.title: Who can manage this database
who.description: People and tokens on this platform with abilities on this database, from their own abilities and from IAM policies.
who.emptyBody: Only users and tokens with platform wide abilities can manage this database.

grant.title: Grant access to this database
grant.description: Applies a policy scoped to this one database. Nothing else on the platform is affected.

templateHint.database-read-only: Can see the database and read its data. Any change is denied.
templateHint.database-operator: Read data and run operations: backups, stop and start. Not users, restore or the write console.
templateHint.database-owner: Everything on this database including users, credentials and network rules.

network.title: Network
network.description: How this database can be reached, who is allowed in, and how far its reach extends.
network.loadFailed: Could not read this database's network: {{error}}

reach.title: Reachability

verdict.stopped: The database is not running, so nothing can reach it.
verdict.privateNone: Private: no app references it and no port is published.
verdict.privateOne: Private: only 1 app can reach it.
verdict.privateMany: Private: only these {{count}} apps can reach it.
verdict.restricted: Published on port {{port}}, restricted to the allowed sources.
verdict.exposed: Exposed to the internet on port {{port}}.
verdict.hostOnly: Published on port {{port}}, but only the host itself can reach it.
verdict.unknown: Published on port {{port}}. The firewall could not be read, so exposure is unknown.

reach.notPublished: Not published. Only containers on a shared Docker network can connect.
reach.makePrivateBody: The database container is replaced without the published port and any rule for it is removed. Apps on the platform keep working. Tools on your machine lose direct access.
reach.madePrivateToast: The port is no longer published
reach.bridgeCaveat: Containers on Docker's default bridge on this host can still reach this database by its address. Scope limits which apps the platform attaches, not what shares the default bridge.

rules.title: Allowed sources
rules.description: Only these addresses can connect to the published port. Rules live in the host firewall and are tagged so they can be removed cleanly.
rules.noPort: Nothing is published, so there is nothing to restrict. Publish a port from Overview to connect from your machine, then lock it down here.
rules.empty: No restriction. Anyone who can route to the published port can connect.
rules.localContainers: Also allow containers on this host
rules.driftMissing: Missing from the firewall: {{sources}}. Apply the rules again to restore them.
rules.driftExtra: The firewall also allows: {{sources}}. These were not set here.

scope.title: Network scope
scope.description: Limits which apps the platform attaches to this database. The default keeps today's behaviour.

hint.platform: Any app that references this database can reach it.
hint.project: Only apps in the database's project. Others are detached.
hint.environment: Only apps in the database's environment. Others are detached.

scope.placement: This database is in project {{project}} and environment {{environment}}.
scope.noneLost: Every app that references this database keeps access.
scope.lost_one: {{count}} app would lose access. It is detached on the next reconcile and shows why on its status.
scope.lost_other: {{count}} apps would lose access. They are detached on the next reconcile and show why on their status.

tls.title: Require TLS
tls.description: Refuse connections that are not encrypted. Connection strings from this platform already ask for TLS.
tls.unsupported: This engine has no TLS requirement setting.
tls.notEnabled: TLS is not enabled for this database yet.
tls.redis: This engine only accepts TLS connections once TLS is on.
tls.drift: The server does not match the saved setting. Toggle it again to realign.
tls.warning: Clients configured with sslmode=disable will be refused.
tls.failedToast: Could not change the TLS requirement
tls.serverHint: Turns TLS on or off on the database server. Turning it off removes the certificate, and the database restarts to apply the change.
tls.switchedToast: TLS setting saved, the database will restart

reveal.title: Reveal password
reveal.description: Shows the generated owner password once on request. It is audited and hides itself after 30 seconds.

rotation.title: Owner password
rotation.description: The password your apps use to reach this database. Rotating it changes the password in the database, checks a real login, then updates every app that uses it.
rotation.unsupportedTitle: Rotation is not available for this engine
rotation.unsupportedBody: This engine runs without an owner password the platform can change, so there is nothing to rotate here.
rotation.pendingBody: A rotation is still settling. It finishes on its own within the hour, and the old password keeps working until then.
rotation.failedBody: The last rotation was rolled back and the old password is still in use. Reason: {{reason}}. You can rotate again.

reason.verify_failed: the database refused the new password
reason.apply_failed: the database could not apply the new password
reason.reference_update_failed: the stored credential could not be updated
reason.interrupted: the rotation was interrupted before the database changed

rotation.willRestart_one: This app restarts to pick up the new password: {{apps}}.
rotation.willRestart_other: These {{count}} apps restart to pick up the new password: {{apps}}.
rotation.noRestart: No running app uses this database, so nothing restarts.
rotation.verifies: The new password is checked with a real login. If that fails, the old password is put back and nothing else changes.
rotation.suspended: Stopped apps pick up the new password when they start: {{apps}}.
rotation.loading: Checking which apps use this database.
rotation.previewFailed: Could not check which apps would restart.
rotation.confirmDescription: Apps restart briefly while they switch to the new password. The change is recorded in the audit log without the password.
rotation.scheduleNext: Rotates automatically every {{days}} days. Next on {{date}}.
rotation.scheduleOff: Automatic rotation is off. Enter a number of days to turn it on.
